title: Progressive compatibility router & name-resolution heuristics for tool/function interop
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers use two dominant calling patterns in the wild: legacy JSON 'functions' used by older SDKs and OpenAI-style 'tools' with schema-first names and structured params. We see mismatches at three layers: 1) naming collisions (case/namespace variations), 2) parameter shape differences (flat vs nested), and 3) runtime routing (which model/variant accepts which surface). Current ad-hoc shims are brittle and leak into client code (many customer issues around tool resolution failures and silent fallbacks).

Proposal: Implement a progressive compatibility router in the runtime that performs (A) deterministic name-resolution heuristics, (B) shallow signature normalization, and (C) a pluggable compatibility layer that can apply translation adapters per-organization or per-route. The router is staged: parse incoming call metadata, run the name-resolution pipeline (exact -> alias map -> fuzzy rules -> canonical fallback), then select a translation adapter which emits a normalized internal contract consumed by the runtime and by downstream shims.

Goals: Reduce customer-facing incompatibility errors by 80% for mixed traffic, allow safe, incremental migration of customers to OpenAI-style tools, and centralize translation logic so we can reason about latency and correctness trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime exposes a compatibility router config controlling name-resolution order and thresholds. 2) Default alias map covers existing legacy-function names for top 50 customer tool names. 3) Normalization adapters transform legacy flat params into typed structured params for 95% of in-scope function signatures. 4) No regressions in latency P50 > 10ms added at runtime under typical load (1000 rps). 5) E2E tests for both legacy and OpenAI-style calling succeed in CI.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (PoC): build a lightweight router in the API gateway that implements exact and alias lookup and returns resolution metadata (can-resolve, resolved-name, adapter-id). Phase 2: implement signature-normalization adapters in the runtime sidecar with a small DSL for mapping flat->typed fields and field renames. Phase 3: admin UI + config APIs to manage alias maps and adapter assignments per-route. Phase 4: telemetry (error rates, resolution latencies) and rollout controls.
rollout_plan: - Start with internal traffic in canary: route 5% of internal calls through compatibility router with translation enabled. - Open beta for specific customers with opt-in flag and dataset of their function names. - Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% for opt-in customers. - Default: start with read-only resolution (router returns suggestions but does not translate) for 2 weeks, then enable automated translation.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for name-resolution heuristics including edge cases (Unicode, punctuation, suffix/prefix variants). - Property tests for adapter DSL to ensure round-trip invariants. - Load tests measuring added latency and memory from route metadata. - Customer regression harness: replay recorded tool calls from top 20 customers and assert identical outputs post-translation or acceptable diffs per tolerance config.
migration_notes: We will publish a migration guide for customers explaining alias mapping and recommended canonical names. For customers using legacy SDKs we provide a minimal client-side shim that can emit 'name_hint' metadata to accelerate the router's resolution. For long-term, encourage adoption of structured OpenAI-style tools; provide an automated mapping export to help customers update manifests.
discussion: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting — agreed on staged approach; Alexis to own alias map generation script.
2025-02-20: PoC prototype validated: alias lookup + adapter selection works on gateway, 6ms median resolution overhead.
2025-02-27: Security review scoped — only metadata and mapping tables are mutable; full secret handling unchanged.
2025-03-02: Ran replay of 12k tool calls from live traffic: 92% were auto-resolvable with first-pass heuristics; remaining cases need per-customer aliases.
2025-03-03: Blocker noted — adapter DSL needs explicit array/tuple mapping to correctly convert legacy positional args. Miguel assigned to design language extension.
